facts.statement: The only described species of Arcovenator is Arcovenator escotae.
facts.quote: The type and only described species is Arcovenator escotae.

facts.statement: The name Arcovenator comes from the river Arc near where the fossils were first found.
facts.quote: Its name derives from the river Arc flowing near the site of its first discovery.

facts.statement: Arcovenator was described by Tortosa and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: parent_authority: Tortosa et al., 2014

facts.statement: Arcovenator lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous,

facts.statement: While initially estimated at 5 to 6 meters long, Arcovenator was later estimated in 2016 to be 4.8 meters long.
facts.quote: it was thus initially estimated as being about 5 – 6 m long, but it was estimated in 2016 as being 4.8 m in length.

facts.statement: Arcovenator has a unique midline foramen on its skull roof that may have housed the pineal gland.
facts.quote: The skull roof exhibits as a unique diagnostic character a midline foramen, possibly housing the pineal gland, situated on the posterior surface of a slight dome formed by frontal bones

facts.statement: Ridges on the parietal bones of Arcovenator's skull fuse to form a sagittal crest.
facts.quote: The parietal bordering the supratemporal fenestrae forms ridges medially on the latter's respective anteromedial margins which, as they approach the parietal eminence, fuse into a sagittal crest.

facts.statement: The postorbital bone of Arcovenator is unique because a sheet of bone links its ventral and posterior processes, placing it between the T-shape of Eoabelisaurus and the inverted L-shape of Carnotaurus.
facts.quote: The postorbital is intermediate between the plesiomorphic T-shaped condition of Eoabelisaurus and the derived inverted L-shaped one of Carnotaurus due to the unique feature of having a sheet of bone linking its ventral and posterior processes.

facts.statement: Arcovenator possesses a thick, rough-surfaced bony brow ridge extending from above the eye socket to the lacrimal bone.
facts.quote: It has, in a similar autapomorphic fashion, a thick, rough-surfaced process dorsal to the eye socket that extends to the lacrimal, forming a bony brow ridge

facts.statement: Arcovenator has remarkable accessory dorsal and ventral bony bars on its paroccipital processes that bound depressions next to the foramen magnum.
facts.quote: The paroccipital processes have remarkable accessory dorsal and ventral bony bars, that thus bound depressions lateral to the foramen magnum.

facts.statement: Arcovenator's tall teeth, measuring 3 to 5.5 cm, feature denticles on both the mesial and distal carinae with varying density.
facts.quote: The tall teeth (3-5.5 cm) have denticles on the apical portion of the mesial carina and along the length of the distal one, with varying density.

facts.statement: Arcovenator has a well-developed cnemial crest on its slender 51-cm tibia, a trait characteristic of abelisauroids.
facts.quote: The cnemial crest of Arcovenator's the slender 51-cm tibia is well developed as is characteristic of abelisauroids.

facts.statement: Arcovenator is classified as a theropod genus within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Arcovenator is a theropod genus nested within the clade Abelisauridae, which in Linnaean taxonomy has the rank of family.

facts.statement: European abelisaurs are divided into a basal lineage (Genusaurus, Tarascosaurus) and a derived lineage including the larger Arcovenator, which is allied with Majungasaurus and Rajasaurus.
facts.quote: Two lineages of European abelisaurs are discerned: a basal one, including the small Albian Genusaurus and Lower Campanian Tarascosaurus, and a derived one, the larger Campanian Arcovenator allied with the Madagascan Majungasaurus and the Indian Rajasaurus in Majungasaurinae.

facts.statement: It is debated how European abelisaurs arrived in Europe, with vicariance suggested for older lineages and oceanic dispersal likely for the more recent derived lineage including Arcovenator.
facts.quote: As the inferred character distributions obtained through the phylogenetic analysis make it unlikely that these lineages are more closely related to each other than to other abelisaurids, this suggests a more complicated series of events regarding their biogeography with vicariance applicable to the older one and oceanic dispersal being likelier for the more recent one.

facts.statement: Fossils of Arcovenator were discovered near Pourrières in southeastern France during pre-construction surveys for the A8 motorway.
facts.quote: The fossil remains of A. escotae were found near Pourrières, Var department, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur region, during preventive paleontological and archaeological prospection activities before construction took place on the stretch of the A8 motorway between Châteauneuf-le-Rouge and Saint Maximin.

facts.statement: Arcovenator lived between 72 and 76 million years ago in the Aix-en-Provence Basin of southeastern France.
facts.quote: The pertinent late Campanian strata (between 72 and 76 million years ago) of the Lower Argiles Rutilantes Formation are located in the Aix-en-Provence Basin of southeastern France.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a braincase, skull fragments, a tooth, a tail vertebra, a tibia, and a fibula found together in fluvial sandstone.
facts.quote: The holotype of Arcovenator escotae, housed at the Muséum d'Histoire Naturelle d'Aix-en-Provence, was found closely associated in a single stratum of fluvial sandstone and is made up of specimens MHNA-PV-2011.12.1, a braincase in articulation with a right postorbital, MHNA-PV-2011.12.2, a left squamosal, MHNA.PV.2011.12.15, a tooth, MHNA.PV.2011.12.5, MHNA.PV.2011.12.5, an anterior caudal vertebra, MHNA.PV.2011.12.3, a right tibia, and MHNA.PV.2011.12.4, a right fibula.

facts.statement: The nearly complete skull suggests Arcovenator was between 5 and 6 meters long.
facts.quote: Aunque poco profundo, el casi completo neurocráneo de Arcovenator es de tamaño similar al de Majungasaurus y Carnotaurus, lo que implica que se trata de un animal de entre 5–6 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The skull roof features a unique diagnostic trait: a central foramen that likely housed the pineal gland on a small dome formed by the moderately thick frontal bone.
facts.quote: La bóveda craneana muestra una única autapomorfia o rasgo de diagnóstico, un foramen situado en el medio, que posiblemente alojara a la glándula pineal, situada en la superficie posterior de un pequeño domo formado por el hueso frontal que es moderadamente grueso como en Aucasaurus, más delgado que el de Rajasaurus y mayor que el de Rugops.

facts.statement: Its teeth are tall, measuring 3 to 5.5 centimeters, and feature denticles along the mesial and distal ridges.
facts.quote: Los dientes son altos (3-5.5 centímetros) tienen dentículos sobre la parte apical de la carena mesial y a lo largo de la longitud de la carena distal, de densidad variable.

facts.statement: The thin tibiae possess a well-developed cnemial crest that is 51 centimeters long.
facts.quote: La cresta cnemial de las tibias delgadas deArcovenator, de 51-cm de largo, está bien desarrollada como ocurre con otros abelisauroideos.

facts.statement: The fibula is nearly half a meter long and displays anatomical features typical of ceratosaurs.
facts.quote: El peroné de casi medio metro de largo posee los rasgos anatómicos típicos de los ceratosaurios.

facts.statement: Arcovenator inhabited the Ibero-Armorican island, a landmass comprising modern-day France, Spain, and Portugal.
facts.quote: A. escotae lived on the Ibero-Armorican island, a relatively large landmass formed by what are now parts of France, Spain, and Portugal.

facts.statement: The environment featured warm, subhumid climates with marked seasons, where rivers flowed into a perennial lake.
facts.quote: The sediment from these sources flowed along rivers into a perennial lake originating interbedded lacustrine, alluvial and fluvial sediments at the time of Arcovenator, when the climate was warm, subhumid with marked seasons.

facts.statement: Fossils were found in fluvial sandstone alongside hybodonts, turtles, crocodylomorphs, pterosaurs, sauropods, the ornithopod Rhabdodon, and nodosaurids.
facts.quote: The fossil remains were found in one of the formation's various levels of fluvial sandstone, characteristic of a river's mouth or when it overflows its banks, along with hybodonts, the turtles Foxemys and Solemys, the crocodylomorphs Musturzabalsuchus and Ischyrochampsa, azhdarchid pterosaurs, titanosaurian sauropods, the ornithopod Rhabdodon and nodosaurids.

facts.statement: The abundance of fragmentary remains, especially teeth, suggests that medium-sized abelisaurids were relatively common in the landscape.
facts.quote: The abundance of fragmentary remains of medium-sized abelisaurs, especially teeth in this and other localities of the region show that these animals would have been relatively common in the landscape.

facts.statement: A single maxilla found at Pourcieux is likely referable to Arcovenator based on its proximity in time and space and phylogenetic analysis.
facts.quote: It is likely that a maxilla, the sole fossil found of the so-called Pourcieux abelisaurid, is referable to at least this genus on account of both its close proximity in time and space and the results of the phylogenetic analysis.
